source.summary: Reduce the tar cat's wings while preserving the person and MoSoCanvas typography.

changes.instruction: Reduce both wings and keep their origin anatomically attached to the cat's back.
changes.reason: Smaller wings reduce collision with the seated figure and integrate the cat into the composition.

preserve.invariant: Keep identity, pose, skin, crop, lighting, and silhouette unchanged.
Keep wording, capitalization, geometry, spacing, position, and tonal treatment unchanged.

prohibit.outcome: The reduced wings still overlap a large portion of the person's arm.
prohibit.consequence: The cat remains visually pasted on and the foreground hierarchy stays confused.

relationships.subject: aggressive tar cat
relationships.relation: contrasts with but does not occlude
relationships.intended_effect: The cat supplies alert tension while the person remains the quiet primary mass.
relationships.pass_condition: The cat reads as tense at normal size, while the person's arm silhouette remains substantially unobstructed.

verification.method: Compare parent and child at use scale and inspect the cat-person boundary.
verification.pass_condition: Both wings are visibly smaller and no large overlap with the arm remains.

verification.method: Overlay the child against the parent and visually inspect identity and title geometry.
verification.pass_condition: No visible drift appears in the seated person, title, or orbital line.
